correctness.rationale: For each graph automorphism of K_{2,n}, a fixed acyclic graph vector field is a g-equivariant directed rooted forest; signed simplicial Lefschetz trace equals (-1)^{n+1} times alternating count by selected edge orbits (including the empty forest). For g=(1,sigma), every nonfixed right orbit contributes 1-1-1=-1; fixed part is determinant det(I-L(K_{2,f}))=(-1)^{f-1}(f^2-1), with f=0 treated separately, producing sgn(sigma)(f^2-1). For g=(swap,sigma), classify right fixed orbits, 2-cycles, longer even cycles and odd cycles to obtain (-1)^{n+1}sgn(sigma)(1-f+2t). For permutation augmentation U_n, χSym²U=(f²-f+2t)/2 and χ(wedge²U+2U)=(f²+f-2t-2)/2; sum/difference reproduce both group characters, with parity-dependent swap of S2 eigenspaces. The claim is an unconditional virtual Euler character; actual homology module only conditional on separately proven nonequivariant degree-n concentration. Independently enumerated all invariant acyclic parent assignments for selected n=3,4,5 permutations, with and without swapping the two distinguished vertices: all 18 samples matched both character formulas exactly. Finite cases corroborate but do not replace the all-n orbit-case count.
residual_risks: Actual homology module is conditional on an independent all-n nonequivariant concentration proof; virtual character itself does not depend on this input.

Scoville–Zaremsky connectivity theorem and Donovan–Scoville star-cluster homotopy results do not determine this full representation for all n.

value.rationale: A closed uniform rational group-character formula and central eigenspace modules for a canonical graph family are a meaningful equivariant refinement of already known wedge/homology ranks. The formula distinguishes representations with identical Betti numbers and provides all group-element traces rather than a single finite instance.
residual_risks: The previously published complete n=4 characterization is not newly valued; increment is the all-n theorem.

final_claim: For every n>=3, exact S2×Sn equivariant reduced Euler character of the ordinary K2,n Morse complex, equal to sgn(sigma)(f²−1) for identity on the degree-n part and (-1)^(n+1)sgn(sigma)(1−f+2t) for its swap, and its parity-dependent rational virtual representation; actual top homology interpretation conditional on known concentration.
limitations: No claim of integral representation lattice or equivariant homotopy classification.
Uniform orbit-forest proof is analytic/combinatorial; finite n=3..5 tests are corroborative only.
